title: A culture of discipline
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What kind of culture does your way of leading create?

Jose said that once a small team is contaminated with negative language, negative belief and victimization, you have to cut off the whole limb. He has seen it in construction: one person says it isn't fair, another jumps on, and soon they are all victims.

A student said it is their perception of the world, and that it comes from another person who did the same. Jose said: it is coming from somewhere, but you can break the generational cycle of victimization.

Jose said the person in the book won't allow someone to say something negative. He is identifying negative belief systems. He wants possibility thinkers. He is building a culture, using fear, and Jose asked what other instruments he has.
A student said it is building a culture around discipline rather than motivation. Jose said: it's discipline, it's relentlessness.
He said the tug of war, the tension, is how he thrives, and the same was said of other famous entrepreneurs.
A student said: you have to compromise with yourself, whether you value empathy or high achievement more. Which way will you lean? A five might not be anything significant, a seven might be.

Jose said you have to decide where you want to be on the spectrum and be honest with yourself. He says people ask him; he tells them: if you are not reaching your goals, there is a reason, and it is a negative pattern in something you are doing.
A student said: it is all internal. What are you doing to yourself to eliminate yourself from that possibility?

Jose said that what he likes is the message: there are no limits. A leader who won't accept a limit gets turnover, and it is self-perpetuating. He said you would have to choose whether that leadership suits you.
What culture do you want, and what will it cost?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the culture you want your team to feel.
Write the language you will not allow, and why.
Write where you are on the spectrum between empathy and high performance.
Write what you will do when someone says they have a limit.
Write what your style costs in turnover and what it gains.

check.q: What did a student say the culture is built around?
What did Jose say about a victim mindset in a team?
choices: It spreads, so you may need to cut off the whole limb

check.q: What did Jose say you must be about where you stand?

recap: Choose your culture on purpose. Be honest about your place on the spectrum.
